headline: エンジン is borrowed from English “engine”.
モーター is the English word “motor” in katakana.
郡, “country, district”, is a Middle Chinese borrowing (MC gjunH).
ハイキング is the English word “hiking” in katakana.
The source says 瓦, “roof tile”, is probably from Sanskrit, possibly via Middle Chinese.
プラスチック is borrowed from English “plastic”.
泡, “bubble, foam”, appears in the Nihon Shoki of 720 CE, from Proto-Japonic *awa.
バイオリン is borrowed from English “violin”.
ナイロン is borrowed from English “nylon”.
濠, “moat”, is the continuative stem of the verb 掘る (horu, “to dig”).
ビルディング is borrowed from English “building”.
知らせ, “notice”, is literally “letting [someone] know”.
ボール covers “ball” and “bowl”, each borrowed from its own English word.
指す, “to point”, is cognate with 刺す (sasu).
ストッキング, “stockings”, is borrowed from English “stocking”.
差, “difference, variation”, comes from Middle Chinese, and the source gives it five readings there.
サンプル is borrowed from English “sample”.
ピクニック is borrowed from English “picnic” and first attested in 1908.
寮, “hostel, dormitory”, is a Middle Chinese borrowing (MC lew).
ロビー is borrowed from English “lobby”.
The source calls 先々週, “2 weeks before”, an abbreviation of 先先週.
シーツ is the English word “sheet” in katakana.
近々 doubles 近 (chika) and voices the second half to jika by rendaku.
トレーニング is the English word “training” in katakana.
質, “quality, nature”, is a kan'on reading, so a later borrowing from Middle Chinese.
レインコート is borrowed from English “raincoat”.
テスト is the English word “test” in katakana.
In 仕様, the character 仕 is ateji for し, the continuative form of する.
ブラウス is borrowed from English “blouse”.
錆びる, “to rust”, is cognate with 荒びる and 寂びる.
メンバー is the English word “member” in katakana.
